A 5-by-7 transpose avoids vector and tiled alignment, exercising scalar rank-2 address mapping.

An aligned 4-by-4 bool tensor uses u32 storage and exercises vectorized tiled transpose without requiring subnormal preservation.
The rank-5 permutation [4,2,0,3,1] scrambles all nontrivial strides and exercises generic scalar gathering.
A rank-7 default transpose (no perm) reverses all seven dimensions through the generic transpose path.

A rank-1 identity transpose with 16,777,217 elements requires 65,536 workgroups and therefore a two-row scalar dispatch. The odd element count exercises the final-row bound and makes a dropped tail element observable.
An aligned [8,8] transpose with perm=[1,0] must carry NaN, both infinities, and zeros exactly to their transposed positions.
With perm omitted, the default full reversal [3,2,1,0] maps output[l,k,j,i] to input[i,j,k,l]. NaN and both infinities must land exactly at their reversed positions.
NCDHW-to-NDHWC transpose with four channels and 32 spatial positions checks exact batched copy semantics.

A rank-5 NDHWC-to-NCDHW transpose (perm [0,4,1,2,3]) moves the size-4 channel axis to position 1, with the D, H, and W dimensions (2x4x4=32 elements) kept contiguous; distinct linspace values at every position make a wrong index mapping observable.
